summary.text: A 24-year-old man with an ordinary birth and normal growth, who worked in a corporation after university and had no family members with psychiatric or developmental disorders, developed insomnia, irritability and anxiety at age 23, followed by agitation, incoherent speech, persecutory delusions and paranoid ideation. Psychiatric assessment confirmed auditory hallucination, suspiciousness, social avoidance and social decline, and paranoid schizophrenia was diagnosed.

Physical, neurological, laboratory, EEG, CT and MRI findings showed no abnormality. Quetiapine was started, with symptoms continuing one week later and significant worsening, and risperidone 12 mg/day and olanzapine 20 mg/day were added without any improvement; treatment-resistant schizophrenia was diagnosed.

At age 24 he developed severe tiredness, fever, joint pain, gingival bleeding and shortness of breath and was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. A 7-day test isolation with all neuroleptics stopped showed he could tolerate isolation, and bone marrow transplantation was performed, with 34 days in an isolation room without neuroleptics, a stable psychotic status and no trouble. Methotrexate and cyclosporin A were begun, and three weeks after BMT early GVHD symptoms were followed by tacrolimus in place of cyclosporin A.

After BMT his psychotic symptoms fell remarkably without neuroleptics and his social functioning improved; thirty days later the psychotic symptom had almost disappeared. Follow-up at 2 and 4 years after BMT showed persistent improvement, and in 2017, 8 years after BMT, he had no residual psychiatric symptoms, recovered social functioning and continued to work. The authors report no infection during the remission of psychosis.
